- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and forecasts too high for next 5–10 days; cap forecast at +5–10% above recent peak or use moving average smoothing.
- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast decline rate or add 1–2% downward bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–7 days ahead); apply 1–3% upward bias for first 7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias after 10–15 days if no new sentiment shift.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -1.0 for 3+ days), model tends to ignore sentiment and forecast flat; adjust downward by 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
